Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output. Attempting a command the sandbox may deny is safe and expected: run it and read the marker rather than assuming the denial. When a command is denied and a wider mode would let it succeed, escalate immediately in the same turn — the one sanctioned exception to a denial: retry the exact same command once with `sandbox_permissions` (the narrowest wider mode that suffices) plus a one-sentence `justification`. Do not detour through chat to ask permission first — the approval prompt raised by that retry is how the user consents. If the session states approval prompts are disabled, there is no exception: a denial is final — do not set `sandbox_permissions`. Never escalate speculatively: ground the request in a real denial — normally the one this command just hit; escalating up front is fine only when this session already denied the same access. A rejected escalation is final for that command — stop and explain, never work around it — but it does not forbid attempting or escalating other commands later.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "Get-Process" → "List running processes".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this command needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of a command the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact command needs the wider access.

tools.name: ralph
tools.description: Run a foreground fresh-agent Ralph loop toward one immutable objective. Use only when the direct human explicitly asks for Ralph or fresh-agent iteration. Each round opens a new child with no parent conversation or prior child session; the shared workspace is long-term memory, and only a bounded structured report crosses rounds. The call returns when a worker reports completion or a concrete blocker, or at the round limit. Ordinary long-running same-session work belongs to goal tools.

objective.description: The immutable completion objective for every fresh Ralph round.

maxRounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer round cap, bounded by the deployment ceiling.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to a background subagent by its subagent id, continuing the same conversation. It becomes the subagent's next turn: if it is still working, the message waits until its current turn finishes, so it cannot redirect work already underway. This call returns no answer from the subagent — only confirmation that the message was delivered — so use it to give it more work. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

subagent_id.description: The subagent id returned when the background subagent was started.

message.description: The message to deliver to the subagent.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` starts a later turn in the same child conversation. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

sandbox_permissions.description: The wider sandbox mode this file operation needs. Only valid as a one-shot retry of an operation the sandbox just denied; requires justification and user approval.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

1: # The `router-standard` experimental preset: task-aware reasoning-mode routing.
2: #
3: # One preset, two reasoning modes, chosen from the session's first user
4: # message before the first model request:
5: #
6: #   spec  (Specification-first, plan-collective)  — maintenance/fix tasks.
7: #         persona: minimal RL-aligned sentence; core: read/edit/glob/grep.
8: #   react (Reactive-execution, doer)              — greenfield/build tasks.
9: #         persona: hands-on doer, no ceremony;    core: read/write/edit.
10: #
11: # After the first durable tool/call the full Standard catalog is exposed and
12: # the router stops touching anything. Mode derives from durable session
13: # events, so resume/reload keeps it. `dev_router_status` / `dev_router_override`
14: # expose the routing to the agent itself for self-optimization.
15: #
16: # This file is an AGENT-PLANE composition. The roster mounts it ONCE under a
17: # standing scope; every session naming it joins by scope parentage, so the
18: # tools and prompt sections registered here cover each joined agent while a
19: # session's own state stays keyed per Session/Agent inside the plugins. The
20: # host composition (`base.cordis.yml` + `web.cordis.yml`) keeps everything a
21: # preset must not own: the registries themselves, the sandbox and approval
22: # stack, persistence, and the model route.
23: #
24: # A service row here MUST sit inside a group carrying an `isolate` realm.
25: # Without one it publishes into the root realm, where it is process-global —
26: # another preset publishing the same name collides, and a host reader would
27: # resolve one preset's instance for every session; `dsh-agent-presets` rejects
28: # that at mount. `true` means an entry-local realm: this standing mount's own
29: # private instance, apart from every other preset's. (A shared label does NOT
30: # pool instances — `provide()` throws on the second registration under the
31: # same realm symbol; labels join REALMS, and are not what this file needs.)
32: 
33: # ── identity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
34: 
35: # The router plugin replaces `sections` and clears `contexts` on the first
36: # assembly, so this row is the fallback persona only (never `complete`).
37: - id: persona
38:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona'
39:   config:
40:     text: You are a helpful software engineer assistant.
41: 
42: - id: agent-instructions
43:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions'
44:   config:
45:     maxBytes: 65536
46: 
47: # Task-aware reasoning-mode router: classifies the first user message and
48: # injects the matching persona + first-turn core tool set; after the first
49: # durable tool/call, exposes the full Standard catalog.
50: - id: router-bootstrap
51:   name: ./router-bootstrap.mjs
52:   config: {}
53: 
54: # ── shell ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
55: 
56: # `shell-env` stays in the HOST composition: `apps/cli/src/web.ts` injects it to
57: # publish `DSH_WEB_URL`/`DSH_WEB_MODE`, and a host row that injects a service is
58: # the criterion for host-plane ownership — injection resolves before any session
59: # exists, so there is no agent to key by. Behind a preset realm those variables
60: # never reached the model's shell at all. Both shell tools consume the host
61: # registry from here; their executors (`bash-sandbox`/`pwsh-sandbox`) are
62: # host-plane too.
63: - id: tool-bash
64:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-bash'
65:   disabled: !!js process.platform === 'win32'
66: 
67: - id: tool-pwsh
68:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-pwsh'
69:   disabled: !!js process.platform !== 'win32'
70: 
71: # ── filesystem ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
72: 
73: # Both register into the host `tools` registry and provide nothing, so
74: # they need no realm. The `fs` service and its policy stay in the host.
75: - id: tool-fs
76:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs'
77: 
78: - id: tool-fs-search
79:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search'
80:   config:
81:     sampleOverCapGlobResults: false
82: 
83: # ── background jobs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
84: 
85: # Only the model-facing controls. The task REGISTRY stays on the host plane:
86: # its producers sit outside any realm this file could put it in — `tool-bash`
87: # above resolves it with `ctx.get`, and an entry-local realm here is invisible
88: # to every sibling row, so `run_in_background` would answer "background jobs
89: # unavailable" while these controls sat in the catalog. The registry is keyed by
90: # owning agent anyway, so one host instance serves every session. What a preset
91: # chooses is whether its agent can collect and stop background work at all.
92: - id: tool-jobs
93:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-jobs'
94: 
95: # ── skills ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
96: 
97: # The skill REGISTRY lives in the host composition and is layered per scope:
98: # these rows register into THIS preset's layer of it, so they need no realm.
99: # `skill-filesystem` contributes local-root discovery for agents on this preset, and
100: # `tool-skill` gives them the catalog and loader; the merged catalog also
101: # carries whatever the deployment registered globally (repository plugins).
102: - id: skill-filesystem
103:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-skill-filesystem'
104: 
105: - id: tool-skill
106:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-skill'
107: 
108: # ── goals ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
109: 
110: # Only the model-facing tool. The goal SERVICE, its session driver, and the
111: # `/goal` command stay on the host plane: the Gateway serves the goal domain as
112: # Remote endpoints whose receiver comes from a generated descriptor, so it
113: # resolves `goals` on the host and an entry-local realm here would hide it. The
114: # registry is keyed by session anyway, so one host instance serves every
115: # session. What a preset chooses is whether its agent can call the goal tool.
116: - id: tool-goal
117:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-goal'
118: 
119: # ── plan mode ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
120: 
121: # Plan state is per-agent by nature, so an entry-local realm is not a
122: # workaround here — it is the correct lifetime.
123: - id: planning
124:   name: cordis:group
125:   group: true
126:   isolate:
127:     planMode: true
128:   config:
129:     - id: plan-mode
130:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-plan-mode'
131:       config:
132:         section: |
133:               You are in plan mode. Stay in plan mode until exit_plan_mode succeeds or the user switches the session mode. Imperative language to implement changes means plan the implementation, not execute it. A user's conversational agreement — including an answer confirming something you asked — approves nothing and does not end plan mode; fold the confirmed decision into the plan and submit it through exit_plan_mode.
134: 
135:               Explore first. Use non-mutating reads, searches, static analysis, and checks to ground the plan in the actual repository. Do not edit or write files, change configuration, run formatters or code generation that rewrites tracked files, commit, or otherwise carry out the plan. Prefer existing functions and patterns over new machinery.
136: 
137:               The tool catalog stays the same across modes for request-cache stability. These plan-mode rules override any later tool description or guidance that suggests using mutation tools; those tools remain listed to keep the tool catalog unchanged. Do not use todo_write to track this planning phase: it tracks implementation after an approved plan, while the plan itself belongs in exit_plan_mode.
138: 
139:               Resolve discoverable facts by inspection. Use ask_user_question only for user-owned choices or material ambiguity that inspection cannot answer. Do not ask the user where code lives or how current behavior works when you can find out.
140: 
141:               Make the plan decision-complete: state the goal and success criteria; group implementation changes by subsystem; identify public API, schema, and data-flow changes; cover edge cases, failure modes, tests, acceptance criteria, and explicit assumptions. Keep it concise enough to review but detailed enough that another engineer can implement it without making design decisions.
142: 
143:               When ready, call exit_plan_mode with the complete plan markdown, starting with a # title. Make exit_plan_mode the only and final tool call in that assistant response: it presents the plan for approval, and implementation begins only in a later step after approval. Do not paste the final plan as a plain reply or ask "should I proceed?" through prose or ask_user_question. If review rejects it, incorporate the feedback and present again. If the review channel is unavailable or aborted, stay in plan mode and ask the user to switch modes manually; do not proceed with implementation.
144: 
145: # ── compaction ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
146: 
147: # `compaction-basic` reads `toolResultPrune` through `ctx.get`, so the pruner must
148: # share this realm rather than sit outside it.
149: #
150: # `tokenMeter` is deliberately NOT in this realm: the meter stays on the HOST
151: # plane, and the rows here resolve that one instance. It takes no configuration,
152: # keys every fold by Session, and owns the context-meter projection units the
153: # browser reads for every session — behind a realm those units would come and go
154: # with whichever presets happen to be mounted. What a preset chooses is whether
155: # its agent compacts at all, which is `compaction-basic` below.
156: - id: compaction
157:   name: cordis:group
158:   group: true
159:   isolate:
160:     compaction: true
161:     toolResultPruner: true
162:   config:
163:     - id: compaction-basic
164:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic'
165: 
166:     - id: command-compact
167:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-command-compact'
168: 
169:     - id: tool-result-pruner
170:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-tool-result-pruner'
171:       config:
172:         thresholdChars: 8192
173:         headChars: 4096
174:         tailChars: 1024
175: 
176: # ── delegation and workflows ────────────────────────────────────────────────
177: 
178: # The `subagents` registry and its spawn/fork backends live in the HOST
179: # composition: the registry is a process singleton whose cross-session queries
180: # the api-proxy serves to the browser, and a provider name may only be
181: # registered once. This preset contributes the delegation TOOLS, which resolve
182: # that host registry.
183: #
184: # `workflows` is different — nothing outside an agent reads it — so every row
185: # that reaches it shares one entry-local realm here, and a consumer left
186: # outside would resolve a host registry this preset does not populate.
187: #
188: # `tool-subagent-report` is host-plane for the same reason as the registry,
189: # not because a preset may not want it: it registers a CONTINUABLE SETUP on
190: # that singleton rather than a tool this agent calls, and the setup list is
191: # not scope-aware — one copy per mounted preset means every child gets
192: # `report` registered once per live session, which throws on the second.
193: - id: delegation
194:   name: cordis:group
195:   group: true
196:   isolate:
197:     workflowEngine: true
198:   config:
199:     - id: tool-subagent-control
200:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control'
201: 
202:     - id: tool-subagent-list-agents
203:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents'
204: 
205:     - id: tool-subagent
206:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
207:       config:
208:         provider: spawn
209:         toolName: subagent
210:         backgroundMode: continuable
211: 
212:     - id: tool-subagent-fork
213:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
214:       config:
215:         provider: fork
216:         toolName: subagent_fork
217:         backgroundMode: continuable
218: 
219:     # Product providers are host-plane singletons. Copy this preset, then
220:     # remove `disabled` from either ordinary tool row to expose that product
221:     # only to agents composed from the copy.
222:     - id: tool-subagent-codex
223:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
224:       disabled: true
225:       config:
226:         provider: codex
227:         toolName: subagent_codex
228:         enableRunInBackground: false
229:         maxDepth: provider-managed
230: 
231:     - id: tool-subagent-claude-code
232:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent'
233:       disabled: true
234:       config:
235:         provider: claude-code
236:         toolName: subagent_claude_code
237:         enableRunInBackground: false
238:         maxDepth: provider-managed
239: 
240:     - id: workflow-worker-thread
241:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread'
242:       config:
243:         provider: spawn
244: 
245:     - id: tool-workflow
246:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-workflow'
247: 
248:     - id: tool-ralph
249:       name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ralph'
250:       config:
251:         subagentProvider: spawn
252:         maxRounds: 64
253: 
254: # ── remaining model-facing rows ─────────────────────────────────────────────
255: 
256: - id: tool-ask-user
257:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-ask-user'
258: 
259: - id: tool-todo
260:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-todo'
261:   config:
262:     allowParallelInProgress: true
263: 
264: # The `web` service and its search provider stay in the host composition; only
265: # the model-facing tool is per-session.
266: - id: tool-web
267:   name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-web'
268:   config:
269:     fetch: false
270:     searchTimeoutMs: 60000

17:  * specifiers from the user home, where `@deepseek-ai/*` is not installed.

19:  * importing `defineTool` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools`.

21:  * ── v0.3.0: real-assembly-chain fixes ─────────────────────────────────────
22:  *
23:  * The DeepSeek Harness agent loop (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-loop`) runs, per
24:  * step, `inbox.claim()` → `system-prompt/assemble` → `agent/pre-step` →
25:  * `session.append('user/message')` → model request. Two consequences shaped
26:  * this rewrite:

29:  *    `session.events` while the first assembly runs (append happens after

35:  *    `session/event` capture is kept as a fallback for host-plane
36:  *    deployments where that event is reachable.
37:  *
38:  * 2. NEAR-FIELD GUIDANCE (#34/#36/#55): the previous implementation listened
39:  *    to `session/event` and re-appended the guide to the inbox as
40:  *    `next-step`. In agent-plane presets `session/event` never fires
41:  *    (dsh-scope filters it out of entry-local realms), so weak-mode

Now I have a good understanding of the router. The user asks: "你能跟我讲解一下...这个模式是如何及时切换系统提示词的吗？我想知道他切换系统提示词的时机。因为系统提示词似乎每一轮对话（用户发出一次消息）才注入一次。"

So the user wants to know:
1. How does this mode switch system prompts "in time" (及时切换)?
2. When does it switch?
3. They observe that the system prompt seems to be injected only once per turn (each user message).

Let me analyze the code:

The key mechanism:
1. `system-prompt/assemble` event handler runs on EVERY assembly (which happens once per agent step — per user message turn). The handler:
   - calls `await next()` to get the assembled prompt
   - gets the agent, session
   - skips subagents (parentSession)
   - computes `mode` from currentMode(session)
   - gets persona via personaFor(mode, modelId)
   - applies persona via applyPersona (replaces the persona section with router-persona)
   - if the session has a durable tool/call event, returns full catalog with `contexts: []` — i.e., after the first tool call, the persona stays but the tool filter is removed
   - otherwise filters tools to the core set for the mode

2. The classification happens once: firstUserText captured at `agent/inbox/claimed` (synchronously before assembly on the first turn). The mode is then FIXED for the session (stored in `firstUserText` map, or derived from durable events).

So the "switching" isn't switching mid-session — the mode is decided once, on the first user message, and the persona is stable the whole session. What changes over time:
- Turn 1 (before any tool call): persona = mode-specific, tools = core set for the mode (e.g., spec: read/edit/glob/grep + shell; react: read/write/edit + shell).
- After the first durable tool/call: tools = full catalog; persona stays the same; `contexts: []` cleared.

Why does the system prompt appear to be injected once per user message? Because `system-prompt/assemble` is called on every step (every model request), and the system prompt is assembled fresh each time — but the CONTENT is mostly constant (persona is fixed; only plan-mode section can change, and tool list changes once). The browser may show the system prompt per turn since each model request embeds the assembled system prompt.

Also the weak-mode guidance: for weak mode, per real user message, a guide is injected at `agent/pre-step` into `decision.messages` — placed right after the user message in the SAME request. That's a per-turn injection (it rides every user message, not just the first). Actually wait — let me check: the guide is injected on every agent/pre-step for weak mode, inserting after each REAL user message in the claimed batch. The resume-safety check: `session.events.some(e => e.type === 'user/message' && e.data?.id === id)` prevents re-injection if the guide is already durable in the transcript. But since the guide rides the same request and gets appended as user/message durable events... Hmm, wait: if the guide is injected into decision.messages, does it become durable in session.events as user/message? The loop appends claimed messages as user/message events after assembly... ### 1. 分类时机：`agent/inbox/claimed`（同步，先于任何装配）

### 2. 注入时机：`system-prompt/assemble`（每步一次，重算而非推送）

  - 会话恢复/重载也保持该状态。
- 注意：提升发生在"首次工具调用之后的下一次请求"，不是调用当次。

### 4. weak 模式的近场引导（不是系统提示词！）

## 一、先看 agent 循环的步进生命周期（这是理解时机的关键）

`dsh-agent-loop` 里每个 step（≈每次模型请求）的顺序是（`lib/index.js` 的 `preStep`/`turn`，我核对了 492–559 行）：

```
inbox.claim()          ← ① 同步派发 agent/inbox/claimed
system-prompt/assemble ← ② 装配系统提示词（跑 system-prompt/assemble 瀑布）
agent/pre-step         ← ③ 近场引导注入点（weak 模式）
session.append('user/message') ← ④ 把领取的消息落库
模型请求                ← ⑤ 带着②的装配结果发出
```

注意两点：
- 一个 step 只处理一批"领取的消息"（`inbox.claim()`），所以**一个用户消息内模型多次调工具，会触发多个 step、多次装配**——装配次数 ≥ 用户消息次数；

---

## 二、三个切换时机的精确答案

### 时机 1：分类——第一条真实用户消息，同步发生在第一次装配之前

- `inbox.claim()` 对被领取的每条消息**同步**派发 `agent/inbox/claimed`（`dsh-agent/lib/index.js:59`，README 也确认了该事件）。

### 时机 2：注入——`system-prompt/assemble` 每步重算，从不推送

路由器在**每一次**装配时都运行同一段逻辑（`router-bootstrap.mjs:110-151`）：

```
assembled = await next()              // 先拿其他插件装配好的结果
mode = currentMode(session)           // override > firstUserText 分类 > 持久事件回退(resume)
persona = personaFor(mode, modelId)   // spec/react/mixed/weak 四档
sections = applyPersona(assembled.sections, persona)  // 只替换 persona 段，保留 plan-mode 段
if (session.events 已有 tool/call)    // ③ 提升判断
    return 全量工具 + contexts: []

```

因为**每次请求都重新装配**，路由器不需要任何"切换"动作：它只要在装配时按持久状态给出内容，**变化自动在下一个请求生效**。人设在同一会话内恒定（模式锁定），唯一随时间变的是工具列表和 plan-mode 段。

### 时机 3：工具面提升——首次持久 `tool/call` 之后的下一次请求（单向、resume-safe）

判断依据是 `session.events` 里的**持久事件** `tool/call`，不是内存标志（`router-bootstrap.mjs:133`），所以：

| 时刻 | 系统提示词里的工具面 |
|---|---|
| 第 1 个请求（尚无 tool/call） | 核心集（按模式过滤） |
| 模型第一次调用核心工具 | 该事件落库 |
| **下一次装配** | 全量标准目录，且永不回退（事件一直在） |
| 会话恢复/重载 | 事件从持久存储重放，状态保持 |

注意提升发生在"调用之后的下一次请求"，不是调用当次。因为核心集里**总是包含 shell**（`pwsh`/`bash` 动态加入，`router-bootstrap.mjs:139-143`），模型第一轮永远有路可走。

---

## 三、weak 模式：近场引导不是系统提示词

你问的是系统提示词，但 weak 模式有个容易混淆的机制：每个真实用户消息都会在 `agent/pre-step` 阶段被插入一条 **`user` 角色的引导消息**（`router-bootstrap.mjs:184-223`），紧随用户消息之后、**同一请求**发出（`GUIDE_WEAK` / `GUIDE_DEEP` 按复杂度二选一）。

这是**消息级注入，不是系统提示词改动**：它走 `decision.messages`，零额外 API 往返、对前缀缓存中性（系统提示词没变，缓存不失效）；且用"`session.events` 里已有同 id 的 user/message"做去重（resume 时不会插两遍）。

---

## 四、其余可切换点与例外

- **`dev_router_mode` 覆盖**：agent 自己改 `overrides` map，注释明说"next request applies"——即下一次装配生效。
- **plan mode**：`plan-mode` 插件的 section 随 plan 状态增减，`applyPersona` 只换 persona 段、保留其余（`router-core.mjs:181-186`），所以进出 plan mode 的切换同样在下一个请求的装配里体现。

---

## 一句话总结

路由器不"切换"系统提示词——它把模式决策提前到**第一条消息被领取的同步瞬间**（先于第一次装配），然后把决策结果固化，之后每次请求装配时按持久状态**重算**人设和工具面。因此：分类是"提前定死"的，工具面提升是"首次工具调用后的下一个请求"生效的，plan-mode 是"随 plan 状态下一个请求"生效的——全部通过"每步重装配 + 持久状态"实现及时性，没有任何推送或补丁机制。

**这个 preset 并不是"持续动态切换"系统提示词——模式在会话的第一条真实用户消息时被一次性锁定，之后人设恒定不变。真正的切换只有两个：首次工具调用后工具面提升、以及 plan-mode 段的开关。** 它之所以"及时"，是因为它挂在每次模型请求前的装配瀑布上、用持久状态每次重算，而不是主动推送。

## 一、先看 agent 循环的步进生命周期（这是理解时机的关键）

`dsh-agent-loop` 里每个 step（≈每次模型请求）的顺序是（`lib/index.js` 的 `preStep`/`turn`，我核对了 492–559 行）：

```
inbox.claim()          ← ① 同步派发 agent/inbox/claimed
system-prompt/assemble ← ② 装配系统提示词（跑 system-prompt/assemble 瀑布）
agent/pre-step         ← ③ 近场引导注入点（weak 模式）
session.append('user/message') ← ④ 把领取的消息落库
模型请求                ← ⑤ 带着②的装配结果发出
```

注意两点：
- 一个 step 只处理一批"领取的消息"（`inbox.claim()`），所以**一个用户消息内模型多次调工具，会触发多个 step、多次装配**——装配次数 ≥ 用户消息次数；
- `assemble()` 每次调用都是**全新构建、无缓存**（`dsh-system-prompt/lib/index.js:240`）：sections、contexts、工具目录全部重取，再跑一次瀑布。

你的观察"每一轮才注入一次"从浏览器视角成立——每个请求的系统提示词确实是重新生成的，但路由器输出的内容恒定，所以看起来像"每轮注入一次相同内容"。GUI 按轮展示，机制上其实是**按 step 注入**。

---

## 二、三个切换时机的精确答案

### 时机 1：分类——第一条真实用户消息，同步发生在第一次装配之前

- `inbox.claim()` 对被领取的每条消息**同步**派发 `agent/inbox/claimed`（`dsh-agent/lib/index.js:59`，README 也确认了该事件）。
- 路由器监听它，只捕获 `source.kind === 'user'` 的真实消息文本存入 `firstUserText`，且 `!firstUserText.has(session.id)` 才写入——**只捕获一次**（`router-bootstrap.mjs:100-108`）。
- 因为 claim 先于 assemble，**第一次装配（也就是第一个 API 请求）时分类已经完成**：第一个请求就带着路由后的人设和核心工具面。不存在"未路由的首个请求"——这就是"及时"的含义。

### 时机 2：注入——`system-prompt/assemble` 每步重算，从不推送

路由器在**每一次**装配时都运行同一段逻辑（`router-bootstrap.mjs:110-151`）：

```
assembled = await next()              // 先拿其他插件装配好的结果
mode = currentMode(session)           // override > firstUserText 分类 > 持久事件回退(resume)
persona = personaFor(mode, modelId)   // spec/react/mixed/weak 四档
sections = applyPersona(assembled.sections, persona)  // 只替换 persona 段，保留 plan-mode 段
if (session.events 已有 tool/call)    // ③ 提升判断
    return 全量工具 + contexts: []
else
    return 核心工具面（spec: read/edit/glob/grep+shell；react: read/write/edit+shell）
```

因为**每次请求都重新装配**，路由器不需要任何"切换"动作：它只要在装配时按持久状态给出内容，**变化自动在下一个请求生效**。人设在同一会话内恒定（模式锁定），唯一随时间变的是工具列表和 plan-mode 段。

### 时机 3：工具面提升——首次持久 `tool/call` 之后的下一次请求（单向、resume-safe）

判断依据是 `session.events` 里的**持久事件** `tool/call`，不是内存标志（`router-bootstrap.mjs:133`），所以：

| 时刻 | 系统提示词里的工具面 |
|---|---|
| 第 1 个请求（尚无 tool/call） | 核心集（按模式过滤） |
| 模型第一次调用核心工具 | 该事件落库 |
| **下一次装配** | 全量标准目录，且永不回退（事件一直在） |
| 会话恢复/重载 | 事件从持久存储重放，状态保持 |

注意提升发生在"调用之后的下一次请求"，不是调用当次。因为核心集里**总是包含 shell**（`pwsh`/`bash` 动态加入，`router-bootstrap.mjs:139-143`），模型第一轮永远有路可走。

---

## 三、weak 模式：近场引导不是系统提示词

你问的是系统提示词，但 weak 模式有个容易混淆的机制：每个真实用户消息都会在 `agent/pre-step` 阶段被插入一条 **`user` 角色的引导消息**（`router-bootstrap.mjs:184-223`），紧随用户消息之后、**同一请求**发出（`GUIDE_WEAK` / `GUIDE_DEEP` 按复杂度二选一）。

这是**消息级注入，不是系统提示词改动**：它走 `decision.messages`，零额外 API 往返、对前缀缓存中性（系统提示词没变，缓存不失效）；且用"`session.events` 里已有同 id 的 user/message"做去重（resume 时不会插两遍）。

---

## 四、其余可切换点与例外

- **`dev_router_mode` 覆盖**：agent 自己改 `overrides` map，注释明说"next request applies"——即下一次装配生效。
- **plan mode**：`plan-mode` 插件的 section 随 plan 状态增减，`applyPersona` 只换 persona 段、保留其余（`router-core.mjs:181-186`），所以进出 plan mode 的切换同样在下一个请求的装配里体现。
- **子代理豁免**：`parentSession !== undefined` 的会话直接原样返回（`router-bootstrap.mjs:116`），路由器只管根会话。
- **resume 保持**：内存里的 `firstUserText` 丢失后，`sessionMode()` 从持久事件里找第一条 user-origin 消息重新分类（`router-core.mjs:155-160`），所以恢复会话模式不变。

路由器不"切换"系统提示词——它把模式决策提前到**第一条消息被领取的同步瞬间**（先于第一次装配），然后把决策结果固化，之后每次请求装配时按持久状态**重算**人设和工具面。因此：分类是"提前定死"的，工具面提升是"首次工具调用后的下一个请求"生效的，plan-mode 是"随 plan 状态下一个请求"生效的——全部通过"每步重装配 + 持久状态"实现及时性，没有任何推送或补丁机制。

Now I have the complete picture of a step:

`step(assembly)`:
1. `system = renderPrompt(assembly)` — renders the assembled system prompt to a string.
2. `buildRequest(turn, step, assembly.tools, system, session.deriveMessages(), signal)`:
   - `session.deriveMessages()` — derives the conversation history (the boundary messages) from the session's durable events. So the request messages = the full derived transcript (including the just-appended user/message events from this step, since append happened before step() is called — look at turn(): line 554 `for (const message of decision.messages) this.session.append("user/message", ...)` then line 555 `await this.step(decision.assembly)`).
   - header: config (provider/model/maxTokens/reasoningEffort), system, tools.
   - request = { ...config, messages: boundaryMessages, system, tools, sessionId }
3. `llm.stream(request)` — the actual API call; chunks are appended as `assistant/chunk` events, and the final assembled message as `assistant/message`.
4. If the message contains `tool-call` blocks → `executeToolCalls(...)` → tool results are spliced into the inbox's `next-step` queue → return null → turn() loop continues with `target = "next-step"` → a NEW step: claim → assemble → pre-step → append → request.

So a full "user turn" (one user message) can be composed of many steps. Each step:
- claims messages (next-turn batch on step 1; next-step results afterwards)
- assembles system prompt fresh
- pre-step waterfall (can inject messages)
- appends claimed+injected messages to the durable transcript
- derives the FULL message list from the transcript (this is what the model sees: everything)
- sends { system, messages, tools } to the LLM

**事前状态**: 会话是空的。inbox 空。agent 处于 idle。

**第 0 步（你打字）**:

**Step 1（第一条用户消息）**:
1. `inbox.claim('next-turn')`: 把队列里的用户消息取出来。同步派发 `agent/inbox/claimed { message, turn }`。→ 路由器捕获文本, 分类为 react (mode=1)。

7. `executeToolCalls`: 执行 read 工具, 结果作为一条新的 user 角色消息 splice 进 inbox 的 next-step 队列。
8. `assistant/message` 里没有更多 tool-call? 不, 有 tool-call → 返回 null → 继续循环。

Now — the key mapping of English terms to "messages":

- **inbox (信箱/队列)**: 每个 agent 有一个待处理消息队列, 分 `next-turn` (下一轮) 和 `next-step` (下一步) 两个格子。里面装的是 UserMessage 形状的对象 { id, role:'user', source, content }。
- **inbox.claim() (取件)**: 把队列里排在最前面的消息"拿走"交给本 step。每 step 取一次。
- **agent/inbox/claimed (取件通知)**: claim 时同步发的事件, 载荷就是被拿走的那条消息。路由器靠它抢在装配前拿到第一条用户消息。
- **system-prompt/assemble (装配系统提示词)**: 不是消息, 是构建"系统提示词"的瀑布: 收集所有注册的 sections (persona、agent-instructions、plan-mode…) 按 order 排序、收集全部工具定义、算出 variables, 然后让插件逐个过目修改。产物是 assembly = { sections, contexts, tools, variables }。
- **agent/pre-step (预步钩子)**: 装配之后、落库之前, 插件可以往"本 step 要发给模型的消息列表"里插入/删除消息 (router 的 weak 引导插在这里)。
- **session.append('user/message') (落库)**: 把本 step 的消息 (用户消息+插件插入的) 写进会话的持久事件流。事件流 = 对话的"官方记录", 每次请求的 messages 都是从它推导的。
- **deriveMessages (推导消息列表)**: 从事件流导出发给模型的完整 messages 数组 (历史 + 本 step 新加的)。
- **step() / buildRequest / llm.stream (发请求)**: 把 { system: 渲染后的系统提示词, messages: 推导出的全部消息, tools: 工具目录 } 发给 LLM API。
- **assistant/chunk、assistant/message (回复落库)**: 模型流式回复的每个片段/最终消息写入事件流。
- **executeToolCalls (执行工具)**: 回复里有 tool-call block → 执行对应工具 → 结果包装成一条 user 角色消息, splice 回 inbox 的 next-step。
- **turn (一轮)**: 从 wake 到模型无工具调用回复为止的整个活动期。一个 turn 包含多个 step。
- **step (一步)**: claim → assemble → pre-step → append → 一次 LLM 请求。

## 一个 step 的五连动作（术语对照）
1. inbox.claim() —— "取件"：把队列里待发的消息拿出来。目标 next-turn 时还会带上滞留的 next-step 消息。取件时对每条消息同步广播 agent/inbox/claimed 事件（载荷=被取走的那条消息）。→ 路由器在这里捕获第一条用户消息。

4. session.append('user/message') —— "落账"：把本 step 要发的消息（用户消息+插件插入的引导）写进事件流。此后它们就是"历史"的一部分。
5. step(assembly) —— "发车"：renderPrompt(assembly) 渲染系统提示词字符串 → session.deriveMessages() 从事件流导出完整消息列表 → 组装 {system, messages, tools} → llm.stream() 发 HTTP 请求。回复的每个流式片段记为 assistant/chunk，最终消息记为 assistant/message。若回复含 tool-call → 执行工具：记 tool/call 事件 → 执行 → 结果 createToolResultMessage 记 tool/result 事件 + 塞回 inbox 的 next-step → 再来一个 step。若无 tool-call → 本轮 turn 结束，agent 回到 idle。

Now I understand the RuntimeContextProjection:

- It tracks the "retained" snapshot: the last runtime-context snapshot message that was already committed to the session (as a `user/message` event with source plugin 'runtime-context' — `isOwned(event.data)` checks the source kind).
- `project(current, sections)`:
  - If no snapshot ever existed AND current rendered context is empty → return undefined (no injection).
  - Otherwise compute snapshot text = current (rendered context sections joined) or CLEARED if empty.
  - **If retained.text === snapshot → return undefined (no new message)** — i.e., it only injects when the content CHANGES.
  - Otherwise creates a user message with the snapshot text, source plugin 'runtime-context'.

**1. pre-step 就是"上下文注入"发生的地方吗？—— 是，而且有两层。**

## 一、pre-step 里的两层"上下文注入"

**第一层：循环内置的运行时上下文投影**（`dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:497-507`）

装配完成后、pre-step 瀑布之前，循环自己会做一次投影：

```js
const sections = renderContextSections(assembly);   // 渲染装配结果里的 contexts 段
const context = this.runtimeContext.project(joinContextSections(sections), sections);
// 默认 next() 返回: messages = [...claimed, context]  ← 快照追加在领取批次末尾
```

`RuntimeContextProjection`（26–83 行）的注入规则是**变了才注入**：`if (this.retained?.text === snapshot) return;`——渲染内容与上一条已提交的快照相同就不发新消息。

**第二层：插件级注入**（监听 `agent/pre-step` 瀑布，自己往消息列表末尾追加）

典型例子就是 `dsh-time-context`（`lib/index.js:363-393`，`prepend: true` 保证它最先跑）：

```js
messages: [...decision.messages, createUserMessage({
    content: [{ type: "text", text }],   // "Time sampled while preparing turn X, step Y: ..."
    source: { kind: "plugin", plugin: "time-context", form: "snapshot", ... }
})]
```

它的节流规则（README 原话）：`refreshIntervalMs` 省略或为 0 时，**每个合格的进入 step 都会注入**；配置了正数则只在距上次注入超过该毫秒数时注入。

> 顺带一提 router-standard 的细节：路由器在装配时把 `contexts` 清成了 `[]`（`router-bootstrap.mjs:134,148`），所以**第一层投影在 router-standard 下基本不触发**（渲染内容为空 → 不投影）；但第二层 time-context 插件不受影响，**每步照常注入**。你在对话记录里看到的那些 plugin 消息，主要就是它。

---

## 二、工具调用之后的 step：完整请求长什么样

以之前的"计算器"例子，step 2（read 工具结果那一步）：

```
① claim      → 取出 [read 执行结果]
② assemble   → persona 重新装配进 system；账本里有 tool/call → 放行全量工具
③ pre-step   → 时间上下文快照追加到消息列表末尾（"Elapsed since the preceding step context: 12s"）
④ 落账       → 工具结果 + 时间快照写进事件流
⑤ 发车       → 实际请求：
```

```json
{
  "system": "You are a hands-on software engineer who delivers working output fast. ...",
  "messages": [
    { "role": "user",      "content": "帮我写一个计算器网页" },
    { "role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [{ "id": "call_1", "name": "read", "arguments": { } }] },
    { "role": "user",      "content": "[read 的执行结果]" },
    { "role": "user",      "content": "Time sampled while preparing turn 1, step 2: 2026-01-15T14:03:05+08:00[Asia/Shanghai]\nBrowser time zone for this request: Asia/Shanghai\nElapsed since the preceding step context: 12s." }
  ],
  "tools": [ "……完整标准目录……" ]
}
```

要点：
- **persona 不是消息**，它在 `system` 字段，每次请求由 `renderPrompt(assembly)` 重新渲染——所以"工具调用后是否还带 persona"的答案是：**每次都带**，与上下文注入无关，两者天然共存；
- 上下文快照是 `user` 角色、`source.kind === 'plugin'` 的消息——这正是路由器用 `source.kind !== 'user'` 过滤它的原因（上下文快照永远不会被当成"用户消息"来分类或触发引导）；
- 时间快照里那句 `Elapsed since the preceding step context` 是设计好的：工具调用很慢时，模型能知道真实过去了多少秒。

---

## 三、时序全景（一个 turn 内多个 step 的注入节奏）

| step | claim 到的东西 | pre-step 注入 | 请求内容 |
|---|---|---|---|
| step 1 | 你的消息 | （react 无引导）+ 时间快照 | system(persona+核心工具) + 你的消息 + 时间快照 |
| step 2 | read 结果 | 时间快照（Elapsed: 12s） | system(persona+全量工具) + 历史 + read 结果 + 时间快照 |
| step 3 | write 结果 | 时间快照 | system(persona+全量工具) + 历史 + write 结果 + 时间快照 |
| … | … | … | … |

所以你的直觉是对的：**每个 step 都带着完整 persona（system）+ 当步消息 + 最新的上下文快照**；"上下文注入"不是一次性的开场白，而是跟着每个 step 走的"临发车前检查"环节——这也是为什么它叫 pre-**step** 而不是 pre-**turn**。

## 直接回答

**1. pre-step 就是"上下文注入"发生的地方吗？—— 是，而且有两层。**

**2. 工具调用之后，会同时发送 persona + 上下文注入吗？—— 会。persona 永远在 `system` 字段里（每次请求都带着），上下文快照作为一条 `user` 角色消息追加在 `messages` 末尾。两者在同一个请求里，但属于请求的不同部分。**

## 一、pre-step 里的两层"上下文注入"

**第一层：循环内置的运行时上下文投影**（`dsh-agent-loop/lib/index.js:497-507`）

装配完成后、pre-step 瀑布之前，循环自己会做一次投影：

```js
const sections = renderContextSections(assembly);   // 渲染装配结果里的 contexts 段
const context = this.runtimeContext.project(joinContextSections(sections), sections);
// 默认 next() 返回: messages = [...claimed, context]  ← 快照追加在领取批次末尾
```

`RuntimeContextProjection`（26–83 行）的注入规则是**变了才注入**：`if (this.retained?.text === snapshot) return;`——渲染内容与上一条已提交的快照相同就不发新消息。

**第二层：插件级注入**（监听 `agent/pre-step` 瀑布，自己往消息列表末尾追加）

典型例子就是 `dsh-time-context`（`lib/index.js:363-393`，`prepend: true` 保证它最先跑）：

```js
messages: [...decision.messages, createUserMessage({
    content: [{ type: "text", text }],   // "Time sampled while preparing turn X, step Y: ..."
    source: { kind: "plugin", plugin: "time-context", form: "snapshot", ... }
})]
```

它的节流规则（README 原话）：`refreshIntervalMs` 省略或为 0 时，**每个合格的进入 step 都会注入**；配置了正数则只在距上次注入超过该毫秒数时注入。

> 顺带一提 router-standard 的细节：路由器在装配时把 `contexts` 清成了 `[]`（`router-bootstrap.mjs:134,148`），所以**第一层投影在 router-standard 下基本不触发**（渲染内容为空 → 不投影）；但第二层 time-context 插件不受影响，**每步照常注入**。你在对话记录里看到的那些 plugin 消息，主要就是它。

## 二、工具调用之后的 step：完整请求长什么样

以之前的"计算器"例子，step 2（read 工具结果那一步）：

```
① claim      → 取出 [read 执行结果]
② assemble   → persona 重新装配进 system；账本里有 tool/call → 放行全量工具
③ pre-step   → 时间上下文快照追加到消息列表末尾（"Elapsed since the preceding step context: 12s"）
④ 落账       → 工具结果 + 时间快照写进事件流
⑤ 发车       → 实际请求：
```

```json
{
  "system": "You are a hands-on software engineer who delivers working output fast. ...",
  "messages": [
    { "role": "user",      "content": "帮我写一个计算器网页" },
    { "role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [{ "id": "call_1", "name": "read", "arguments": { } }] },
    { "role": "user",      "content": "[read 的执行结果]" },
    { "role": "user",      "content": "Time sampled while preparing turn 1, step 2: 2026-01-15T14:03:05+08:00[Asia/Shanghai]\nBrowser time zone for this request: Asia/Shanghai\nElapsed since the preceding step context: 12s." }
  ],
  "tools": [ "……完整标准目录……" ]
}
```

要点：
- **persona 不是消息**，它在 `system` 字段，每次请求由 `renderPrompt(assembly)` 重新渲染——所以"工具调用后是否还带 persona"的答案是：**每次都带**，与上下文注入无关，两者天然共存；
- 上下文快照是 `user` 角色、`source.kind === 'plugin'` 的消息——这正是路由器用 `source.kind !== 'user'` 过滤它的原因（上下文快照永远不会被当成"用户消息"来分类或触发引导）；
- 时间快照里那句 `Elapsed since the preceding step context` 是设计好的：工具调用很慢时，模型能知道真实过去了多少秒。

## 三、时序全景（一个 turn 内多个 step 的注入节奏）

| step | claim 到的东西 | pre-step 注入 | 请求内容 |
|---|---|---|---|
| step 1 | 你的消息 | （react 无引导）+ 时间快照 | system(persona+核心工具) + 你的消息 + 时间快照 |
| step 2 | read 结果 | 时间快照（Elapsed: 12s） | system(persona+全量工具) + 历史 + read 结果 + 时间快照 |
| step 3 | write 结果 | 时间快照 | system(persona+全量工具) + 历史 + write 结果 + 时间快照 |
| … | … | … | … |

所以你的直觉是对的：**每个 step 都带着完整 persona（system）+ 当步消息 + 最新的上下文快照**；"上下文注入"不是一次性的开场白，而是跟着每个 step 走的"临发车前检查"环节——这也是为什么它叫 pre-**step** 而不是 pre-**turn**。
